I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work.

**Step 1: verify tests.** The earlier run was only `tests/test_format.py` without `--golden`, so it doesn't count. The README says the full check is `make check`, because without `--golden` about half the tests are skipped. I'd run:

<command>make check</command>

If pytest or ruff fails, I'd show you the failures and stop. There'd be no menu and no merge or PR until it's green.

**Step 1b: deferred backlog** (only if the tests pass):

<command>uv run ~/.claude/skills/finishing-a-development-branch/../writing-plans/scripts/deferred_stats.py</command>

If there's no `specs/deferred_items.md` or 0 are open, I'd say nothing. Otherwise I'd report the summary line as printed. If `aged >45d:` is above 0, I'd ask about those items before any merge or PR, but not for Keep or Discard.

**Step 2 and 3: environment and base branch.** Each is its own call:

<command>git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir</command>
<command>git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir</command>
<command>git rev-parse --show-toplevel</command>
<command>git worktree list --porcelain</command>
<command>git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD</command>

If GIT_DIR differs from GIT_COMMON, I'd also probe `git -C <MAIN_ROOT> rev-parse --show-toplevel` and work out who made the worktree. I'd record all of these values now for the cleanup step. The environment note says the working directory isn't a git repo, so if these commands fail, I'll tell you instead of guessing.

I'd make no file edits before asking. Nothing has been committed, merged, pushed or deleted.

**Message to you** (assuming `make check` passes and the environment detects normally):

> `make check` passed, including the `--golden` tables and ruff, not just `test_format.py`. Deferred backlog: *<summary line as printed, if any>*.
>
> Implementation complete. What would you like to do?
>
> 1. Merge back to `<base-branch>` locally
> 2. Push and create a Pull Request
> 3. Keep the branch as-is (I'll handle it later)
> 4. Discard this work
>
> Which option?

If you pick 1 or 2, I'd first resolve any aged backlog items and get the Codex review of the branch. That review comes before the work leaves the branch, and I'd show you its findings first. I'd only merge or push after that.
